attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Internal Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Intermittent left anterior chest discomfort radiating to left shoulder for 3 weeks, worse with inspiration and when lying on left side

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents with recurrent chest discomfort similar to her January 2020 presentation. She describes the pain as sharp, localized to the upper left anterior chest, and occasionally radiating to the left shoulder. The pain is worse with deep inspiration, certain movements of her left arm, and when she lies on her left side at night.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Musculoskeletal chest pain (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her family history is unremarkable.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She works as a graphic designer and spends long hours at a computer.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
She denies shortness of breath, palpitations, syncope, cough, fever, or recent trauma.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, vital signs are normal.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Cardiac auscultation reveals normal heart sounds without murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. There is focal tenderness to palpation over the left costosternal junctions of the second and third ribs, which reproduces her chest pain. No swelling, skin changes, or crepitus are present.

IMAGING:
ECG and chest radiography are normal.
